'''''Picconia excelsa''''', commonly known as '''{{lang|es|palo blanco}}''', '''{{lang|pt|pau blanco}}''', or '''{{lang|pt|branqueiro}}''', is a species of tree in the family [[Oleaceae]]. It is [[endemic]] to [[Macaronesia]], occurring only on [[Madeira]] and the [[Canary Islands]].

==Distribution and habitat==
''Picconia excelsa'' can be found on the island of [[Madeira Island|Madeira]] in the Madeira [[archipelago]] and on the islands of [[El Hierro]], [[Fuerteventura]], [[Gran Canaria]], [[La Gomera]], [[La Palma]], and [[Tenerife]] in the Canary Islands. It primarily occurs in [[laurel forest]]s at altitudes of {{cvt|200-1200|m}} [[above sea level]],<ref name=IUCN/> though it can also be found growing in [[pine]] forests and [[heathland]] dominated by ''[[Myrica]]'' and ''[[Erica (plant)|Erica]]'' species. It is typically found in open areas on slopes or in valleys.<ref name=AC>{{cite web |title=''Picconia excelsa'' |url=https://www.arbolappcanarias.es/en/species/info/picconia-excelsa/ |website=Arbolapp Canarias |publisher=[[Consejo Superior de Investigaciones Científicas]], [[Real Jardín Botánico de Madrid]], and [[Jardín Botánico Canario Viera y Clavijo]] |access-date=23 October 2024}}</ref>

==Description==
''Picconia excelsa'' is an [[evergreen]] [[shrub]] or small [[tree]] growing {{cvt|10-15|m}} tall with a somewhat open [[Crown (botany)|crown]]. The roughly textured [[Bark (botany)|bark]] is white or grey in colour. The leathery [[leaf|leaves]] are [[Glossary of leaf morphology#elliptic|elliptic]] to [[Glossary of leaf morphology#obovate|obovate]] in shape and arranged [[Phyllotaxis|opposite]] one another, each measuring {{cvt|6-8|cm}} long. The leaves are dark green above and paler below, hairless, with entire [[Leaf#Margins_(edge)|margins]]. The [[raceme|racemose]] [[inflorescence]] bears [[Hermaphrodite#Plants|hermaphroditic]] flowers. The flowers are white in colour, sometimes sweet-scented, with four [[petal]]s. The [[fruit]] is a fleshy [[drupe]] with a single seed, similar to an [[olive]], and measures approximately {{cvt|2|cm}} long. The fruit is initially green, becoming purplish black as it [[Ripening|ripens]].<ref name=AC/><ref name=TSO>{{cite web |title=''Picconia excelsa'' (Ait.) DC. |url=https://www.treesandshrubsonline.org/articles/picconia/picconia-excelsa/ |website=Trees and Shrubs Online |publisher=[[International Dendrology Society]] |access-date=27 October 2024}}</ref>

==Ecology==
''Picconia excelsa'' is an important component of the laurel forests of Madeira and the Canary Islands.<ref name=IUCN/> It is known to be a [[host (biology)|host]] for the [[epiphytic]] [[liverwort]] ''[[Frullania polysticta]]'', a laurel forest [[Generalist and specialist species|habitat specialist]] also endemic to Macaronesia.<ref>{{cite iucn |last1=Sim-Sim |first1=M. |last2=Hodgetts |first2=N. |last3=Martins |first3=A. |year=2019 |title=''Frullania polysticta'' |volume=2019 |article-number=e.T39193A87713320 |doi=10.2305/IUCN.UK.2019-2.RLTS.T39193A87713320.en |access-date=27 October 2024}}</ref>

==Conservation status==
Previously assessed as [[vulnerable species|vulnerable]] in 1998, ''Picconia excelsa'' is listed as [[least concern]] on the [[International Union for the Conservation of Nature]]'s [[Red List]] as of 2017 on account of its prevalence throughout its range, its apparently stable population, and the absence of major threats. Current threats include [[invasive species]] and the [[Exploitation of natural resources|exploitation]] of forest resources. This species is present in several [[protected area]]s, including [[Garajonay National Park]] and [[Madeira Natural Park]], and is conserved ''[[ex situ]]'' in at least 25 collections, including a [[seed bank]].<ref name=IUCN/>

==Uses==
The wood of ''Picconia excelsa'' is used locally for [[carpentry]] and construction purposes. It is sometimes planted as part of [[reforestation]] efforts and as an [[ornamental tree]].<ref name=IUCN/> It was introduced to the [[United Kingdom]] as an ornamental species in 1784.<ref name=TSO/>
